inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.name: seed

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: GymFC uses Gazebo v10.1.0 with Dart v6.7.0 as the backend simulator
FlightControlEnv is a generic OpenAI flight control gym environment; a subclass must set the OpenAI gym action_space and observation_space attributes
The constructor connects an asyncio UDP datagram endpoint to the Aircraft plugin's host and port
The simulator starts gzserver with the configured world file
step_sim runs one asynchronous simulation step and returns the flattened observation
reset sends an Action_pb2.Action.RESET message to the simulator and returns the observation
The default configuration selects attitude.world
The configured attitude.world declares the Dart physics engine and a max_step_size of 0.001 s
FlightControlEnv.sdf_max_step_size reads the world's physics max_step_size element and returns its float value as the simulation step size
BaseEnv declares a four-element Box action space between -np.ones(4) and np.ones(4), i.e. -1 and 1
BaseEnv.step maps the action with action_to_control_signal(action, 0, 1), so each element is clipped to [0, 1] before it becomes a motor control signal despite the [-1, 1] action space
action_to_control_signal clips the action to [action_low, action_high] and maps it linearly to [y_low, y_high]
The observation space is an unbounded Box (-inf to inf) with as many elements as the state function returns
BaseEnv.step returns (state, reward, done, {}) and sets done when sim_time reaches max_sim_time
BaseEnv.reset re-initialises the state arrays, resets the simulator and returns state_fn(self); seed() initialises the environment generator through gym.utils.seeding
StepEnv generates step setpoints: it holds a sampled target for pulse_width seconds and then returns to zero
StepEnv.reset samples a new target with the seeded generator as np_random.normal(0, max_rate, size=3)
The registered state function state_degrees_error_deltaerror returns the measured angular-rate error and its delta, six values in total
gymfc_nf-step-v1 is registered with max_rate 100, pulse_width 2.048 s, max_sim_time 4.608 s and that state function
RewardEnv.compute_reward combines an angular-rate error shaping term, control-output and oscillation penalties, an error-band reward and a doing-nothing penalty

determinism.notes: StepEnv.seed() seeds the generator used to draw the next step target, and the fake repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the fake uses Python's random.Random while upstream uses gym.utils.seeding's numpy generator, so one seed gives different trajectories on the two. Gazebo/Dart bit-for-bit repeatability was not tested and is not claimed.

gaps: the fake backend is a reduced analytic stand-in: it models the action clipping, motor mixing and a first-order angular-rate response, not the Gazebo/Dart rigid-body, contact and aerodynamic dynamics of the upstream simulator
no actuator, sensor, noise or battery model is reproduced in the fake; sample_noise is a no-op and the IMU, ESC and battery measurements of the digital twin are not simulated
the fake does not model the UDP protobuf channel, packet drops or timeouts, gzserver startup, or the digital-twin SDF; it was not compared with the upstream simulator
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms only
snapshot and restore are not offered: neither the environment nor the fake exposes get_state/set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
